title: Mixed Vegetable Curry
subtitle: South Indian-style vegetables in a spiced tomato and coconut sauce
excerpt: A vibrant mix of cauliflower, potato, spinach, and chickpeas cooked in a spiced tomato sauce finished with coconut milk. An easy and satisfying vegan curry for any night of the week.

recipe.sourceNotes: This curry draws on South Indian vegetable cooking traditions, where cauliflower, potato, and spinach are staple curry vegetables and coconut milk provides the sauce base. Chickpeas add protein and body. The spice base uses the South Indian combination of mustard seeds, curry leaves, and turmeric alongside cumin and coriander. This is a practical weeknight version rather than a specific regional dish: a reliable framework for any selection of firm vegetables.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to hold all the vegetables comfortably.

content.text: Cut the cauliflower into small florets and the potato into 1.5 cm cubes so they cook in the same time. The spices go in after the onion: they need a minute of direct heat in the oil to bloom before the wet ingredients go in. Add the spinach at the very end: it needs only a minute to wilt and overcooks quickly to a dull, watery mush if added too early.

Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 10 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute.

Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce has thickened slightly. Add the potato cubes and stir to coat. Add 200 ml of water and season with salt. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the cauliflower florets and chickpeas. Stir through. Cover and cook for a further 10 to 12 minutes until both potato and cauliflower are tender. Add the coconut milk and stir through.
Add the spinach in handfuls and stir until wilted, about 2 minutes. Add the garam masala. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice.
